title: PL/pgSQL Procedural Language Basics
description: Understand block structure, variable declaration, control flow (IF/ELSE, CASE), and loops in PL/pgSQL.

data.text: **PL/pgSQL** is PostgreSQL's built-in procedural language. It extends SQL with control structures (loops, conditionals), variables, cursors, and structured error handling.

data.title: Basic PL/pgSQL Structure with Conditionals

data.text: A `FOR ... IN SELECT` loop iterates over the rows of a query and assigns each row to a record variable. It is convenient for per-row work, but each iteration is a separate SQL statement, so it is slower than a single set-based statement. Use it when the work is inherently procedural — calling a function per row, logging, or sending a notification.

data.title: Iterate, raise notices, and aggregate
data.content: The loop accumulates a total and raises a notice for any order above a threshold.

data.title: Prefer set-based SQL when you can
data.text: A loop that reads N rows issues N statements, each with parse and plan overhead, and it holds a snapshot for the whole loop. If the same result can be produced with one `UPDATE`, `INSERT ... SELECT`, or aggregate, that version is faster and easier for the planner to optimize. Reach for the loop only when the logic genuinely cannot be expressed as a set operation.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: PL/pgSQL blocks follow `DECLARE ... BEGIN ... END;` syntax.
